Team Name: Beyond the Flame

We are five Computer Science students passionate about AI, Data Science, and Space Exploration.

Our Skills: AI/ML, Python, NLP, Data Analysis, Web Development, and Research.

Our Project: Exploring microgravity combustion data through AI-powered analysis and interactive visualizations to make scientific findings easier to understand and compare.

Our Mission: Turn space science data into meaningful insights that support innovation and fire safety research in space.
summary:
Flame in Freefall works by processing NASA research papers and experimental data to make microgravity combustion research easier to explore. Users can ask questions in natural language, retrieve relevant scientific evidence with source references, explore NASA investigations, extract experimental parameters, and compare research findings. The platform also provides image and video analysis using OpenCV to examine visible flame characteristics.

It is built using Python, FastAPI, Next.js, React, and TypeScript, with BM25 and TF-IDF for information retrieval, NLP techniques for scientific information extraction, and optional LLM integrations for answer generation.

The goal is to make scattered scientific research more accessible, support evidence-based analysis, and help researchers better understand fire behavior in microgravity. It is currently a research-support prototype, not a certified spacecraft fire-safety system.
details:
Flame in Freefall

Flame in Freefall is an AI-assisted research platform designed to help researchers, students, and aerospace engineers explore and understand how fire behaves in microgravity.

What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

Fire behaves differently in microgravity than it does on Earth. Understanding these differences is important for improving fire-safety research for spacecraft and future space habitats. However, relevant scientific information is often spread across research papers, technical reports, and experimental datasets.

Our platform brings relevant NASA research into one place and makes it easier to explore and analyze.

It provides several capabilities:

  • AI Research Assistant: Users can ask questions in natural language and retrieve relevant scientific information with references to supporting research sources.
  • Scientific Information Retrieval: The platform uses hybrid search techniques, including BM25 and TF-IDF, to find relevant information across research documents.
  • NLP-Based Analysis: We developed scientific information extraction methods to identify important concepts such as fuel, combustion, oxygen, pressure, temperature, soot, and microgravity. We also developed a separate SciBERT-based model prototype for domain adaptation and named entity recognition.
  • Experimental Comparison: The platform provides functionality to explore and compare findings across different research investigations.
  • Image and Video Analysis: Using OpenCV, the platform analyzes visual characteristics of flames, including color, brightness, shape, and changes across video frames.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Flame in Freefall aims to make complex scientific research more accessible and easier to analyze. Instead of manually searching through multiple documents, users can explore relevant studies, retrieve supporting evidence, identify scientific parameters, and compare research findings through a single platform.

Our intended impact is to support a better understanding of combustion in microgravity and contribute to research that may help advance fire-safety technologies for future spacecraft and human space exploration missions.

Tools and Technologies

We developed the platform using:

  • Programming Languages: Python and TypeScript.
  • Backend: FastAPI.
  • Frontend: Next.js and React.
  • Natural Language Processing: Hugging Face Transformers, SciBERT, and PyTorch.
  • Information Retrieval: BM25 and TF-IDF.
  • Computer Vision: OpenCV.
  • Data Processing: Pandas and NumPy.
  • PDF Processing: PyMuPDF.
  • LLM Integrations: Optional integrations with Gemini, Groq, OpenAI-compatible APIs, and Ollama.
  • Development Tools: VS Code, Jupyter Notebook, and GitHub.

What Makes Our Project Creative?

Our project combines scientific information retrieval, NLP, experimental comparison, and computer vision in one research-support platform focused specifically on combustion in microgravity.

Rather than treating NASA research documents as isolated sources, we aim to connect scientific concepts, experimental findings, and visual observations to help users explore relationships between different studies.

Factors We Considered

During development, we considered:

  • Scientific Reliability: Grounding retrieved information in NASA research and providing source references.
  • Research Accessibility: Making complex scientific documents easier to search and understand.
  • Microgravity-Specific Challenges: Focusing on combustion behavior and visual flame characteristics that may differ from those observed on Earth.
  • Technical Feasibility: Building a modular prototype using available NASA research materials and accessible software tools.
  • Transparency and Limitations: Distinguishing between retrieved scientific evidence and AI-generated responses, while recognizing that visual analysis is not a validated physical prediction model.

Our current project is a research-support prototype. It is not a certified spacecraft fire-detection, prediction, or emergency-response system.
